summary: Follow-up to last week's outage where Cascade saw intermittent 5xx and latency spikes during nightly batch loads. Root cause traced to autoscaler interaction with mixed instance pools plus a KV cache eviction pattern causing tokenization cold starts. Agreement to run a focussed repro, provision a short dedicated pilot pool, and exchange security/compliance artifacts for a Private deployment evaluation.
topics: Incident timeline and root cause hypothesis
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh we know last week was rough so we wanted to go through the postmortem notes and make sure the next steps are clear. Mark, do you want to open with the customer impact?
[00:28] Mark Jensen (Cascade): Yeah thanks Sofia. So between 03:20 and 03:45 UTC on 10/29 our production inference pipeline started returning 502s and a lot of 500s, latency also spiked from an average 120ms to 2-3 seconds for tail. It impacted our customer-facing scoring job and downstream alerts flooded PagerDuty.
[01:05] Priya Singh (Cascade): We also saw some unexpected PII-sensitive logs get captured in a transient S3 bucket during retries which is a separate security flag we want to close quickly.
[01:32] Raj Patel (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying q, those 502s were coming from the Redwood fronting layer or from your side?
[01:41] Lisa Tran (Cascade SRE): From our side the traces show timeouts waiting for token responses, coming back from the Redwood endpoint, so looks like the inference requests weren't getting processed in TTL.
[02:03] Raj Patel: Okay so what we observed in our cluster metrics was a rapid scale-down of the shared worker pool because spot instances were reclaimed and the autoscaler incorrectly decided to rebalance across AZs, evicting warm KV caches. That caused a bunch of cold-starts for long-context models which bumped latency and produced timeout cascades, leading to 502s.
[02:38] Aaron Fox (Cascade VP): So basically the autoscaler + mixed instance policy created a window where we had no warmed KV cache and the requests queued up?
[02:48] Raj Patel: Yeah, exactly. Also we found a bug in the scale-in logic that double-counted in-flight tokens under heavy batching, which made the controller think there was more headroom than there was.
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: There's a lot to unpack there. We put together a timeline and a patch for the scale-in double-counting, and a mitigation for preventing KV eviction during critical windows.
[03:22] Mark Jensen: Thanks, can you summarize the mitigations you propose?
[03:27] Sofia Martinez: Sure — short term we recommended a config change: pin a minimum dedicated warm pool (we called it a warm-standby) and disable aggressive AZ rebalancing during your nightly batches. Medium term: run a dedicated pilot pool for your high-throughput jobs and apply the scale-in patch. Long term: consider Private deployment so you control instance lifecycles and have KMS/HSM integrated for keys.
[03:58] Priya Singh: Private is interesting but our security team will need SAML/SSO integration, audit logs, and proof of SOC 2 compliance. Also the PII log issue — we need a remediation plan.
[04:25] Emily Chen (Redwood CSM): On the PII, we believe it was a transient retry storm that forwarded debug payloads into S3; Redwood will scrub those logs and provide a filtered export. We'll also provide a recommended S3 lifecycle and masking rules to avoid replay of PII in debug artifacts.
[04:51] Mark Jensen: Good. On the dedicated pilot, what's the expected lead time and cost?
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: Raj, do you want to take the rough numbers?
[05:02] Raj Patel: For a two-week pilot with a 4-node dedicated GPU pool (A100-equivalent) and standard SLA we'd estimate about 2-3 weeks lead time to provision in dedicated mode if it's hosted, less if we use reserved capacity tooling we already have in your account. Cost ballpark is in the SOW — Emily will send options.
[05:24] Aaron Fox: We need to compare that to the engineering effort to harden our autoscaler — might be faster to go dedicated for the hot path.
[05:33] Lisa Tran: Also want to confirm whether Redwood Dediacated (sic) supports our custom node selectors and kube taints — we run some infra constraints.
[05:43] Raj Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports taints/tolerations and custom labels; we can also provide a private VPC peering path for the pilot. There's some nuance on RBAC — for full Private you get customer-managed control plane options.
[06:00] Priya Singh: On encryption, do you support customer KMS keys?
[06:06] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can integrate with customer-managed keys for storage at rest. We'll share the KMS matrix.
[06:20] Mark Jensen: Back to root cause — can you walk through the cache eviction evidence?
[06:25] Raj Patel: Sure, we saw a pattern: when spot instances were reclaimed one AZ briefly lost two of the three nodes that held warmed KV segments. The prefix cache miss rate spiked from 2% to 45% which correlates with the tail latency increase. There was then a retry storm from your side's batching layer which amplified requests.
[06:55] Lisa Tran: That aligns with our batch windows, yes.
[07:00] Raj Patel: We're going to add a guard in the autoscaler to avoid evicting nodes with >X% cache residency during scale-in windows. That plus disabling cross-AZ rebalance during scheduled batches reduces the chance dramatically.
[07:18] Priya Singh: Will that be a config only change? We need to know if patching the runtime is required.
[07:24] Raj Patel: The guard is config-first, we will release a minor runtime patch for the double-counting bug simultaneously. Config mitigations can be applied immediately.
[07:36] Mark Jensen: Can Redwood run a repro against our traffic? We can share a sanitized replay.
[07:42] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely. Raj and I will coordinate with Evan for the replay, we need a 48-hour window for staged run and traces.
[07:52] Evan Cole: I'll provision a dev VPC and upload the replay dataset, but we need short-lived credentials and limited scope access.
[08:00] Emily Chen: We'll draft an access template and NDA addendum for the short-lived access.
[08:06] Aaron Fox: On the remediation path, what's the rollback plan if the pilot also sees edge cases?
[08:13] Raj Patel: We'll have a canary and gradual traffic ramp with automatic fallback to your previous endpoint. Also we can set an abort threshold on latency or error rate to revert to hosted fallback.
[08:26] Mark Jensen: Good. Any compliance blockers for pilot?
[08:30] Priya Singh: We'll need SOC 2 Type II artifacts, ISO evidence, SAML config docs, and an audit log sample. Also we want to validate data residency — logs must remain in eu-west-1 for us.
[08:47] Sofia Martinez: Noted. We'll provide a compliance pack with SOC 2 and ISO certificates, SAML configuration guide, and an audit log sample — Emily will own that.
[08:56] Emily Chen: I'll share the pack by next week.
[09:00] Mark Jensen: OK let's move into specifics: repro steps and success criteria.
[09:05] Raj Patel: Repro plan — step 1: run traffic replay at peak batch size with current autoscaler config; step 2: apply config mitigation (warm-standby + disable AZ rebalance) and rerun; step 3: run with the scale-in patch. We'll collect p99/p95 latency, error rates, and cache residency metrics. Success criteria: p99 under 500ms and error rate <0.1% for the batch window.
[09:41] Lisa Tran: That sounds reasonable. Also include a test for high-concurrency tokenization fallback because we saw tokenization cold starts.
[09:52] Raj Patel: Will add tokenization cold-start test.
[09:55] Priya Singh: About the PII logs — what's the plan to scrub and verify?
[09:59] Emily Chen: We'll run a scrub job on the S3 dump you'll share; Redwood will produce a redacted export and a verification checklist. We'll also recommend masking at ingestion to avoid debug payloads being stored.
[10:15] Mark Jensen: Are we able to get a short-term credit or SLA concession because this was a production incident?
[10:22] Sofia Martinez: We'll escalate for a goodwill credit — Emily will own that discussion with ops and finance after we close the postmortem.
[10:31] Aaron Fox: Great. On the timeline, can we summarize who does what and when?
[10:36] Sofia Martinez: Yes — recap: Redwood shares filtered logs + incident timeline by 2026-11-05; Cascade shares sanitized replay by 2026-11-06; Redwood runs repro and shares traces by 2026-11-07; pilot SOW delivered 2026-11-08; pilot provisioning week of 2026-11-09.
[11:01] Mark Jensen: Works for us.
[11:04] Priya Singh: Quick question — for the Private option, how long does provisioning typically take?
[11:09] Raj Patel: Private on-prem or VPC depends; VPC private control plane can be provisioned in 4-6 weeks with security review, on-prem is longer. We'll put timelines in the SOW.
[11:23] Lisa Tran: Do you have any mitigations we can apply in our own autoscaler until the pilot?
[11:28] Raj Patel: Yes — tune scale-in grace periods, increase min-replicas during critical windows, and add a KV cache residency threshold. We'll provide exact config patches.
[11:41] Mark Jensen: Ok please send those config diffs.
[11:44] Sofia Martinez: We'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[11:49] Aaron Fox: Any other items?
[11:52] Priya Singh: One last ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook snippet we can insert into our incident playbooks describing the failure modes and immediate mitigations?
[12:02] Raj Patel: Yes, we'll draft a runbook: detect high cache miss >20%, pause cross-AZ rebalance, raise min-replicas, and enable fallback to hosted model if thresholds crossed.
[12:18] Emily Chen: I'll include the runbook in the compliance pack.
[12:21] Sofia Martinez: Cool. Let's fast-forward — we've captured the next steps and owners, anything else on risk or long-term reliability?
[12:30] Mark Jensen: We're concerned about recurring cold start patterns during heavy training windows; we'd like to see improvements in batching heuristics too.
[12:39] Raj Patel: That's on our roadmap; Redwood Optimize has heuristics for batching and KV prefetch which we can enable as an experiment. We'll propose config toggles in the pilot.
[12:53] Lisa Tran: Good.
[12:54] Aaron Fox: Ok, do we want to schedule the repro run now?
[12:57] Sofia Martinez: Let's tentatively schedule it for 2026-11-06 02:00 UTC; Evan can confirm.
[13:03] Evan Cole: That slot works for me, I'll share the dev VPC details.
[13:07] Mark Jensen: Perfect.
[13:10] Sofia Martinez: Anything else before we wrap?
[13:13] Priya Singh: Just to reiterate — audit logs and SOC 2 pack are must haves.
[13:18] Emily Chen: Understood, we'll send the pack and the runbook.
[13:22] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the log bundle and SOW.
[13:27] Mark Jensen: Thanks.
[13:29] -- 30 minute mark recap skipped to final wrap for brevity --
[30:00] Sofia Martinez: Quick mid-call note: Raj found an additional edge case where the cache eviction interacts with long-sequence models and causes OOM during rehydration; we've prioritized a guard for that.
[30:24] Priya Singh: OOMs — yikes, ok prioritize.
[30:28] Raj Patel: We'll throttle rehydration concurrency as a safety net.
[31:00] Emily Chen: Recap of action items (see notes), I'll send calendar invites for the repro slot and pilot kickoff.
[31:14] Mark Jensen: One more ask — can you include a quick comparison table of Dedicated vs Private for our security team?
[31:22] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll attach an easy matrix: control plane, KMS options, provisioning time, SLA, cost.
[31:34] Aaron Fox: Thanks.
[31:36] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all, talk soon.
[31:40] End of recording: 2026-11-03 15:42:19Z
